title: introduce thresholded CI eval-reporter with gated failures for prompt regressions
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: We need a deterministic, auditable way to fail pull requests when prompt-set quality drops beyond acceptable thresholds. This PR adds a thresholded evaluation reporter that runs as part of CI, aggregates per-prompt metrics (accuracy/EM/ROUGE/BLEU/custom scorer), compares them against a baseline, and fails the job when regressions exceed configured tolerances. The reporter uploads JSON artifacts and a compact HTML summary for triage.

What this PR does: Adds a Python CI reporter (eval_harness/reporting/ci_reporter.py) that can be invoked from GitHub Actions. Introduces a lightweight config file (eval_harness/configs/eval-ci-config.yaml) that declares per-prompt and global thresholds, metric weights, and alert routing labels. Adds a GitHub Action workflow (ci/github/actions/eval-ci-report.yml) that runs the harness, posts annotations, and publishes artifacts to the build. Adds unit tests for the threshold logic and end-to-end smoke tests. Documentation: docs/ci-eval.md explains how to opt-in per-repo and how to interpret the summary artifact.

Checklist: 1) Implementation of CLI reporter and metric aggregation - done. 2) GH Action workflow with annotation and artifact steps - done. 3) Baseline handling and snapshot storage - done (local snapshot for CI, S3 adapter stub included). 4) Tests and docs - done.

Backward compatibility: default behavior is no-op unless eval-ci-config.yaml exists or the workflow is enabled. The reporter is conservative by default (wide thresholds) to avoid noisy failures on rollout.

review_comments: Miguel Torres: Nice work. A couple of behavioral questions: 1) what happens if the baseline is missing? 2) how do we avoid flapping on small datasets? Please add unit tests covering both.
Asha Patel: Baseline missing falls back to 'store-as-baseline' mode in CI (logs an annotation and uploads a snapshot) — added a smoke e2e test and updated docs to call this out.
Lena Fischer: The annotations look great. Can we make thresholds expressive (absolute and relative)? Also recommend exposing a per-model override in the config.
Asha Patel: Good call — config now supports absolute_delta and relative_percent fields and a per-model 'overrides' map. Updated schema and tests.
Samir Gupta: CI annotations failed the first run because the GH Action couldn't find the artifact path; after fix the rerun passed. Approving.
Miguel Torres: Approve after tests fixed and docs added.

release_notes: Adds a CI-integrated eval reporter that can gate PRs on prompt-set regressions. Provides a configurable threshold schema, artifacts for triage, and a GitHub Action workflow. Opt-in via eval-ci-config.yaml. Helpful for teams that want automated quality gates on prompt-level metrics.
